title: A live coding round
objectives: Work a 45-minute live problem with two follow-ups.

screens.title: Which bookings are accepted
screens.prose: A calendar takes a booking `[start, end)`: the start counts, the end does not. A booking is accepted if it overlaps none already accepted. You merged intervals in l1-merging-intervals. New here: a live round that adds rules part-way.
screens.question: Bookings arrive in the order shown, with one booking allowed at a time. Tap the ones that are accepted.

hints.text: Take the bookings one at a time, in order.
The second, `[3, 6)`, starts inside `[1, 4)`.
`[4, 8)` starts exactly where `[1, 4)` ends, and the end does not count. `[0, 1)` also touches without overlap.

feedback.correct: `[1, 4)`, `[4, 8)` and `[0, 1)` are accepted. `[3, 6)` overlaps the first.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. A booking is refused only if it shares a time with one already accepted.

byKey.all: You accepted every booking. `[3, 6)` overlaps `[1, 4)` between 3 and 4.
byKey.i2: `[3, 6)` shares the times 3 with `[1, 4)`, which was accepted first.
byKey.i3: `[4, 8)` starts at 4, and `[1, 4)` does not include 4, so they do not overlap.
byKey.i4: `[0, 1)` ends at 1, and `[1, 4)` starts at 1, so they do not overlap.
byKey.i1: The first booking meets an empty calendar, so it is accepted.

explain.text: `[3, 6)` shares the time 3 with `[1, 4)`, so it is refused. `[4, 8)` and `[0, 1)` only touch it, because the end is not included. Three bookings are accepted.

screens.title: The first five minutes
screens.prose: A live round of 45 minutes is reported to open with five minutes of questions. Choose the one that matters most to the examples.
screens.question: Which question changes whether `[1, 4)` and `[4, 8)` clash?

options.text: Is the end of a booking included?
Can a booking be cancelled later?
options.why: You chose a question for a later stage. It does not change whether these two clash.

options.text: Which language should I use?
options.why: You asked about tools. The ends of a booking decide the examples.

options.text: How many bookings will there be?
options.why: You asked about size. It changes the speed you need, not the answers.

hints.text: Look at where the two bookings meet.
They meet at the time 4.
If the end is included, both hold 4 and clash. If it is not, they do not.

feedback.correct: The end rule decides the examples, so ask it first.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Which question changes an answer you can see?

byKey.b: Cancelling matters for stage C, not for this clash.
byKey.c: The language does not change which bookings clash.
byKey.d: The count changes the design, not the answers to these examples.

explain.text: The two bookings meet at 4. Whether they clash depends on whether the end counts. Ask it first, then whole numbers, then cancellation.

screens.title: Stage A: book
screens.prose: Write `Calendar()` with `book(start, end)`. Keep the starts and ends sorted, and use `bisect` to find the place. The starter accepts everything.

params.title: Calendar
lines: Accept a booking [start, end) if it overlaps none accepted.
Return True if accepted, False if not.
The driver run_cal(k, ops) is hidden: rows [0, start, end] book.

screens.question: Write `Calendar` and `book`.

widget.how: Check runs 6 hidden tests, from the edge of a booking to 60,000 bookings. The driver `run_cal` is hidden.

hints.text: Which two bookings can overlap a new one?
Only its neighbours in the sorted order.
The one before must end by `start`. The one after must start at or after `end`. Use `bisect_left` on the starts.

feedback.correct: Check the left neighbour's end and the right neighbour's start.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Check the first failing test.

byKey.test-2: Test 2: bookings that touch at an end are accepted.
byKey.test-3: Test 3: bookings that fit around each other are accepted.
byKey.test-4: Test 4 did not match. Trace it by hand.
byKey.test-5: Test 5 did not match. Trace it by hand.
byKey.test-6: Test 6 has 60,000 bookings. Scanning every booking each time is too slow.

explain.text: Because accepted bookings never overlap, the sorted order is also the time order. A new booking can clash only with the one before or after its place. Two comparisons settle it.

screens.title: Run stage A by hand
screens.prose: Run stage A on five bookings, with one allowed at a time: `[2, 5)`, `[5, 7)`, `[4, 6)`, `[7, 9)` and `[0, 2)`.
screens.question: How many are accepted?

hints.text: Which booking overlaps an earlier one?
`[4, 6)` starts inside `[2, 5)` and overlaps `[5, 7)`.
The other four only touch at an end, so they are accepted.

feedback.correct: `[4, 6)` is refused. The other four are accepted.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Compare each booking with the accepted ones.

byKey.all: You accepted `[4, 6)`, but it overlaps `[2, 5)` between 4 and 5.
byKey.three: You refused one booking too many. The others only touch at an end.

explain.text: `[2, 5)` and `[5, 7)` touch, so both are accepted. `[4, 6)` overlaps both and is refused. `[7, 9)` and `[0, 2)` only touch, so four are accepted.

screens.title: Stage B: up to k at once
screens.prose: First follow-up: `Calendar(k)` allows up to `k` bookings at any instant. The sorted-list shortcut breaks, because neighbours no longer decide. Complete `_fits`: count the overlaps at the new start and at each booking start inside the new interval.

params.title: Calendar
lines: At most k bookings may cover any instant.
and each booking start inside the new interval.

screens.question: Complete `_fits` so `book` honours `k`.

widget.how: Check runs 9 hidden tests. Four use `k = 1`, and five use `k` of 2 or 3.

hints.text: Where can the number of overlaps rise inside the new interval?
Only at a time where another booking starts.
Check the new start, and every booking start strictly inside the new interval. At each, count bookings with `s <= p < e`.

feedback.correct: Check the start and each booking start inside.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Check the first failing test.

byKey.test-1: Test 1 did not match. Trace it by hand.
byKey.test-2: Test 2 did not match. Trace it by hand.
byKey.test-3: Test 3 did not match. Trace it by hand.
byKey.test-4: Test 4: with `k = 2`, a booking inside two others at time 15 is refused.
byKey.test-5: Test 5: with `k = 2`, `[5, 11)` meets two bookings at time 10.
byKey.test-6: Test 6: with `k = 3`, the fourth booking overlaps three at time 4.
byKey.test-7: Test 7 did not match. Trace it by hand.
byKey.test-8: Test 8: with `k = 2`, `[5, 15)` meets two bookings at time 5.
byKey.test-9: Test 9: with `k = 2`, `[3, 12)` overlaps two bookings, but never at the same time.

explain.text: The overlap count changes only where a booking starts. So it is enough to test the new start and every start inside the new interval. If none exceeds `k - 1`, the booking fits.

screens.title: Two at once
screens.prose: With `k = 2`, bookings arrive in the order `[1, 4)`, `[3, 6)`, `[2, 5)` and `[4, 8)`.
screens.question: How many are accepted?

hints.text: Look at the time 3.
At time 3, `[1, 4)` and `[3, 6)` are both booked.
`[2, 5)` would be a third at time 3, so it is refused. `[4, 8)` starts when `[1, 4)` has ended.

feedback.correct: `[2, 5)` is refused: at time 3 it would be the third booking.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Count the bookings at each start inside the new one.

byKey.all: You checked only the start of `[2, 5)`. At time 3, inside it, two bookings already stand.
byKey.two: You refused `[4, 8)` too. At 4, `[1, 4)` has ended, so only `[3, 6)` stands.

explain.text: `[1, 4)` and `[3, 6)` both fit, as two may overlap. `[2, 5)` would make three at time 3, so it is refused. `[4, 8)` meets only `[3, 6)`, so three are accepted.

screens.title: Stage C: cancel and next_free
screens.prose: Second follow-up: `cancel(start, end)` removes one exact earlier booking. `next_free(duration, after)` returns the earliest whole start at or after `after` where a booking of that length would be accepted. The candidates are `after` and the end of each booking after it.

params.title: Calendar
lines: Remove one exact earlier booking. Return True if it was there.
The earliest whole start at or after `after` where a booking that long is accepted.

screens.question: Add `cancel` and `next_free`.

tests.expect: [True, True, True, True, True, True, True, False]

hints.text: Where can the earliest free start be?
At `after`, or just when some booking ends.
Try `after` and each booking end above it, in order, with `_fits`. Return the first that fits.

feedback.correct: Try `after` and each later end, in order.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Check the first failing test.

byKey.test-2: Test 2 did not match. Trace it by hand.

byKey.test-4: Test 4 did not match. Trace it by hand.

byKey.test-8: Test 8 did not match. Trace it by hand.
byKey.test-9: Test 9: `cancel` must report False when there is no exact match, and remove only one booking.
byKey.test-10: Test 10: a free start is the first candidate where the booking fits.
byKey.test-11: Test 11: after the cancel, the freed time is available again.
byKey.test-12: Test 12: an empty calendar gives `after` itself.

explain.text: A free start only improves when a booking ends, so the candidates are `after` and the ends above it. We test them in order with the same `_fits` check. `cancel` removes the exact pair and nothing else.

screens.title: Cancel and look again
screens.prose: With `k = 1`: book `[9, 12)`, book `[12, 15)`, ask `next_free(3, 9)`, ask `next_free(2, 9)`, cancel `[9, 12)`, then ask `next_free(3, 9)` once more.
screens.question: What does the last `next_free(3, 9)` return?

widget.label: Start
widget.accept: 9: the cancel freed the time from 9 to 12

hints.text: What does the cancel change?
It frees 9 to 12.
A booking of 3 starting at 9 now fits exactly before `[12, 15)`.

feedback.correct: After the cancel, `[9, 12)` is free and `next_free(3, 9)` is 9.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. The cancel removes a booking.

byKey.before: That is the answer before the cancel. After it, the time 9 is free.
byKey.twelve: A booking of 3 at 12 would overlap `[12, 15)`. The free start is 9.

explain.text: Before the cancel, both bookings fill 9 to 15, so the first free start for 3 is 15. The cancel frees 9 to 12. A booking of 3 then fits at 9.

screens.title: Sit a round
screens.prose: Open `#drill`, set the pattern to `intervals` and the difficulty to 4, then pick a Python or C++ drill. The stopwatch counts up from the moment it opens, so keep the 45-minute plan.
screens.question: Which plan fits a 45-minute round with two follow-ups?

Clarify 0, base 25, test 0, first follow-up 10, second follow-up 10, explain 0

options.text: Clarify 15, base 15, test 5, follow-ups 5 and 5, explain 0

Check that the blocks add to 45 and that every follow-up has 10 minutes.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Add the blocks and compare them with the follow-ups.

byKey.c: Questions that long leave only 5 minutes for each follow-up.

screens.title: The 45-minute plan
screens.prose:
A live round has layers. Each layer extends the code you already have.

```python
# 00 clarify, examples        (5)
# 05 base: book              (10)
# 15 test                    (5)
# 20 follow-up 1: k          (10)
# 30 follow-up 2: cancel     (10)
# 40 explain the trade-offs   (5)
```

Test the base against the examples
Explain the design and what you would change at scale

The rules and some examples.
Clarify, base, test, follow-up 1, follow-up 2, explain.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Each layer builds on a tested one.

byKey.p3: Test the base before you extend it.

screens.title: Ten million bookings
screens.prose: The interviewer asks for 10 million bookings, general `k`, and a cost of $O(\log n)$ per booking. The scan costs $O(n)$ and a sorted list pays to shift entries.
screens.question: Which structure meets the cost?

options.text: A tree keeping the largest overlap per time range: $O(\log n)$
A hash map of bookings keyed by start time: $O(1)$ lookups
options.why: You chose a map with no order. It cannot tell the overlap at a time without a scan.

options.text: A heap of end times, popping the earliest: $O(\log n)$ per push
options.why: You chose the earliest end only. A heap cannot count the bookings at an arbitrary time.

options.text: The same list, scanned faster in a lower-level language such as C++
options.why: You kept the scan. A faster scan is still $O(n)$ per booking.

hints.text: What must the structure answer about a time range?
The largest number of overlaps inside it.
A tree that adds on a range and keeps the maximum per part does this in $O(\log n)$.

feedback.correct: A tree with a range maximum answers 'does it fit?' in $O(\log n)$.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. The structure must find the largest overlap in a range.

byKey.b: A hash map has no order, so a range query needs a scan.
byKey.c: A heap gives the earliest end, not the overlap at a time.
byKey.d: Speeding up a scan does not change its cost per booking.

explain.text: A balanced or segment tree keeps the largest overlap per part of the time line. A sorted map of +1 and -1 changes finds the start in $O(\log n)$ but walks the changes inside. Say the cost and the trade-off aloud.

ideas: A live round is reported to run in layers. Clarify, base and test come first, then follow-ups that change a rule or add an operation.
A half-open booking holds its start but not its end. With `k` above 1, test the new start and every booking start inside it.
Keep the 45-minute plan: 5, 10, 5, 10, 10 and 5. Say the cost and the trade-offs of each design aloud.
